sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for The Driver: Judgment, Emotions, Medical Condition and Age

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
Drivers under twenty have about twice the expected crashes, while drivers around fifty to fifty-four have the fewest of any age group [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint age-and-crashes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec05-F09 and sec05-F10.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
Crashes rise again from age fifty-five, but drivers over seventy-five still crash less often than drivers under twenty-five [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint age-and-crashes; prereq_hint sec05-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec05-F11 and sec05-F09.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
Good judgment can compensate for weaker skill or experience, while poor judgment can wipe out even expert skill [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint judgment; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec05-F02 and sec05-F01.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
Emotional upsets such as anger or grief call for a cooling-off period before driving, while worry, illness or fright call for letting someone else drive [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint emotions; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec05-F04 and sec05-F05.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A02
The younger driver's problem is the urge to exhibit and accept challenges, while the older driver's problem is failing to notice declining ability [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint age-problems; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec05-F13 and sec05-F15.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A02
Aging increases reaction time and decision time, while it decreases hearing, eyesight, dexterity and attention span [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint age-problems; prereq_hint sec05-R05; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec05-F14 and sec05-F16.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A01
The driver is the only element of the three that can gather information and act, while the environment and the vehicle are conditions the driver must manage [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint judgment; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec05-F01 and sec05-F07.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A02
Declining a challenge proves maturity, while accepting one proves only inexperience and immaturity [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint age-problems; prereq_hint sec05-R05; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec05-F13 and sec05-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A02
Annual physical examinations and knowledge of medication effects are habits for every driver, while recognizing a gradual decline is the step older drivers most often miss [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint health; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec05-F16 and sec05-F15.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A01
Alcohol, drugs, illness and disability are medical factors that contribute to crashes, while worry, anger and overconfidence are emotional factors that do the same [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint fitness; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec05-F08 and sec05-F03.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0024]
